strings.name: Tsitsi Dangarembga
strings.summary: Dangarembga examines colonial legacies through Black women's education, family and work in Nervous Conditions and its sequels. She also makes films, builds local creative institutions and advocates public freedoms. Convicted over a peaceful protest in 2022, she had the conviction overturned the following year. Literary work and civic action intersect throughout her career.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Writes women's education and postcolonial society through novels such as Nervous Conditions and film, as an important Zimbabwean literary voice.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Mutoko, then Southern Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied medicine at Cambridge, later psychology in Zimbabwe and filmmaking in Berlin.
strings.highlights.h1.title: A trilogy of female development
strings.highlights.h1.text: Nervous Conditions, The Book of Not and This Mournable Body follow Tambu's development within an unequal society.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Art and public freedom
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses fiction, film and public advocacy to examine colonial power, gender and freedom of expression.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussed freedom in Barcelona
strings.timeline.t1.text: Gave an interview during her residency about colonialism, identity and the limits of freedom.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Protest conviction overturned
strings.timeline.t2.text: An appeal overturned the conviction imposed in 2022 over her participation in a demonstration.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published Black and Female
strings.timeline.t3.text: Essays considered race, gender and empire; that year her protest case brought a fine and suspended sentence.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Received two literary honors
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won the PEN Pinter Prize and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade, recognizing her writing and public stance.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published the trilogy's third novel
strings.timeline.t5.text: This Mournable Body appeared and later reached the 2020 Booker Prize shortlist.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Directed Everyone's Child
strings.timeline.t6.text: The feature explored orphaned children and their society, extending her storytelling to the screen.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Nervous Conditions appeared
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her first novel followed a girl's education; it won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize for a first book in Africa the next year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Began medicine at Cambridge
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered medical studies, later leaving the course and returning to Zimbabwe to pursue psychology and creative work.
